Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All evaluable conclusions in the documentation match the results originally recorded. The plan states AIE=6.6% for MLP vs 1.6% for attention, which matches Section 2.2 of the documentation. zsRE results (99.8% efficacy, 88.1% paraphrase, 24.2% specificity) match Table 1. COUNTERFACT results for GPT-2 XL (Score 89.2, 100% efficacy, 96.4% paraphrase, 75.4% neighborhood) and GPT-J (Score 91.5, 99.9% efficacy, 99.1% paraphrase, 78.9% neighborhood) match Table 4 exactly.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All steps from the final plan are reflected in the implementation. Causal Tracing is implemented in experiments/causal_trace.py and demonstrated in notebooks/causal_trace.ipynb. ROME is implemented in the rome/ directory with rome_main.py, compute_u.py, and compute_v.py. Evaluation on zsRE is in experiments/py/eval_utils_zsre.py. Evaluation on COUNTERFACT is in experiments/py/eval_utils_counterfact.py. Both GPT-2 XL and GPT-J are supported via hyperparameter files in hparams/ROME/.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: The reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitudes. For Causal Tracing, MLP AIE of 6.6% is 4x larger than attention AIE of 1.6% at the early site. For ROME on zsRE, efficacy improves by 77.6 percentage points (22.2% to 99.8%). For ROME on COUNTERFACT, the Score of 89.2 represents substantially higher performance than alternatives (FT: 65.1, FT+L: 66.9, MEND: 57.9). These effects are clearly above baseline variability.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices are explicitly justified. The corruption method (noise level 3x embedding standard deviation) is justified in Section B.1 with robustness analysis in Figure 13. Target layer selection is justified through Causal Tracing analysis in Section 2, confirmed by Figure 5 showing peak ROME performance at middle layers matching the AIE peak. The linear associative memory model is justified in Section 3.1 with mathematical derivation. Key vector averaging over 50 random prefixes (Equation 3) and value optimization with essence drift control (Equation 4) are justified with empirical validation showing >80% success rates.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key experimental results report appropriate measures of uncertainty. Table 1 (zsRE) and Table 4 (COUNTERFACT) report 95% confidence intervals for all metrics with clear notation (e.g., '99.8 (±0.0)'). Figure 7 shows line plots with 95% confidence intervals for Causal Tracing results. Figure 5 explicitly states 'Areas show 95% confidence intervals'. Sample sizes are clearly reported (1000 facts for Causal Tracing, 10000 for zsRE, 7500/2000 for COUNTERFACT). The methodology for computing CIs is consistent throughout.
